title: Quantization Profile Library MVP PRD: finalize scope, stakeholder review, and beta sign-off checklist
creator: Aditya Rao
description:
Goal
- Drive MVP PRD to completion for the opt-in Quantization Profile Library and route-level enablement controls.
- Coordinate stakeholder review (Runtime, Platform/Routing, Applied ML/Evals, SRE, Security, Telemetry/Billing, DX/Docs) and capture decisions + open issues.
- Produce a concrete sign-off checklist for beta launch (scope, pricing/packaging, eligibility, support readiness, go/no-go criteria).

Background
Quantization Profile Library will publish Redwood-maintained per-model quantization profiles (fp16/bf16/int8/int4 variants with hardware/kernel constraints, calibration notes, and expected cost/latency deltas). Customers can enable quantization per API route with canary and fast rollback. v1 is Redwood-published only (no user-supplied profiles) and is opt-in.

MVP scope (must be explicitly stated in PRD)
1) Quantization Profile Library (Redwood-published)
- Profile schema + versioning + signed artifacts in model registry
- Clear scoping: model family + model version + quantization method + supported GPU arch/SKU + kernel constraints
- Required metadata: expected perf delta range + known limitations + calibration notes + last validation timestamp

2) Route-level enablement and rollout safety
- Route-level toggle: disabled by default
- Canary support: percentage-based traffic gating per route
- Fast rollback: one-click disable per route (and optionally per customer override if we decide to include in MVP)
- Safe fallback: if incompatibility detected (hardware mismatch, kernel unsupported, missing artifact), automatically fall back to baseline and emit metrics

3) Validation and quality gates (pre-publish)
- Baseline vs quantized comparisons using eval harness prompt sets
- Perf suite runs across sequence length bins and supported GPU matrix
- Approval workflow: Applied ML + Runtime sign-off for initial profiles

4) Telemetry / customer visibility
- Tag execution with profile id/version and path (baseline vs quantized)
- Console visibility: route status + recent regressions + links to dashboards (MVP may be read-only status if write UX not ready)

Non-goals (must be explicit)
- Default-on quantization for all customers
- User-supplied profiles (library is Redwood-published only in v1)
- Fully automated profile generation without human review

Decisions needed (capture in PRD)
A) Beta eligibility / packaging
- Who can access beta: self-serve opt-in vs allowlist (recommended: allowlist for first ~10–20 orgs)
- Any pricing changes: none for beta; measure savings and determine post-beta packaging under Optimize add-on (proposal)
- Dedicated/Private availability in beta: Hosted first; Dedicated/Private gated by compatibility testing and support readiness

B) Control surface definition
- Canonical control: Route config in control plane (not ad-hoc request headers)
- Do we allow per-request overrides in beta? (recommended: no; keep deterministic for observability and rollback)

C) Beta success metrics
- Cost: median tokens/$ improvement on opted-in routes (target: >= 20% on supported profiles without quality gate failures)
- Quality: regression rate (target: < 5% of opted-in routes hit auto-disable due to quality signals in a rolling 7d window)
- Reliability: no increase in 5xx attributable to quantized path beyond +0.05% absolute on opted-in routes
- Adoption: # of orgs enabling + sustained usage over 2+ weeks

D) Support / operational model
- On-call ownership for beta issues: SRE primary + Runtime/Applied ML escalation rotation
- Clear rollback runbook and customer comms template

Deliverables
- Final PRD with: problem statement, goals/non-goals, personas, MVP scope, UX/API behavior, rollout plan, success metrics, beta criteria, risks/mitigations, and launch checklist.
- Stakeholder sign-offs recorded in ticket comments and/or PRD approval section.

Primary reviewers
- Product: Nikhil Sharma, Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes
- Applied ML/Evals: Dr. Maya Srinivasan, Arjun Desai, Jonas Weber, Selene Huang
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez, Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova
- Platform/Routing: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Jordan Lee, Priya Natarajan
- Telemetry/Billing: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Cole Summers
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes
- Security: Marcus Lin
acceptance_criteria: PRD updated with explicit MVP scope vs non-goals (no ambiguity on customer controls, profile publication, and rollout/rollback).
PRD includes beta criteria (eligibility, allowlist process, go/no-go metrics) and a launch readiness checklist.
Pricing/packaging section included: beta pricing stance + post-beta packaging hypothesis + measurement plan.
Stakeholder sign-off captured from Applied ML, Runtime, Platform/Routing, Telemetry/Billing, SRE, Security, and Docs/DX.
Open questions enumerated with owners and dates for resolution (or explicitly deferred with rationale).
signoff_checklist: Scope: MVP definition agreed (Hosted first; Dedicated/Private gating documented).
Controls: route-level enablement semantics + canary behavior specified (including precedence rules if org/customer/route overrides exist in MVP).
Safety: fallback behavior + auto-disable signals documented and aligned with SRE runbooks.
Quality gates: prompt sets + regression thresholds defined; approval workflow defined (who approves publishing a profile).
Telemetry: metrics/tags required for dashboards and billing attribution agreed; owners assigned.
Security: artifact signing/verification + audit logging requirements reviewed; publish permissions model clarified.
Packaging: beta access + support expectations + limits (rate limits / supported models) documented.
Docs: beta docs plan includes opt-in steps, monitoring, rollback guidance, and known limitations.

comments: 2025-01-24 (Talia Benson): Proposed review cadence: Applied ML + Runtime review by 1/31, Platform/Routing by 2/3, SRE/Security/Billing by 2/6. Please add any must-have launch criteria to the checklist section so we don't miss them late.

2025-01-30 (Jonas Weber): PRD should explicitly call out what constitutes a 'quality regression' for tool-calling/JSON routes vs freeform chat. Recommend separate gates or at least separate reporting so we don't block low-risk summarization routes due to structured-output failures elsewhere.

2025-02-01 (Mateo Alvarez): +1 on no per-request overrides for beta. If we allow headers early, troubleshooting becomes impossible and we lose determinism for caching + observability. Route config only; canary via policy eval. Also add explicit requirement: fallback to baseline must be silent to the caller unless they query status/metrics.

2025-02-03 (Nadia Rahman): Pricing section needs a concrete statement: beta does not change invoice rates; we will report estimated savings in Console (non-billable informational). Also ensure cost attribution tags include profile id/version so Finance can audit deltas.

2025-02-04 (Sean Gallagher): SRE needs the PRD to name the rollback trigger set (p95 latency spike, 5xx increase, structured-output parse failure rate, eval gate fail) and what happens automatically vs manually. Recommend: auto-disable per-route when a route crosses a threshold for N minutes, with audit log entry and paging policy.

2025-02-06 (Marcus Lin): For security sign-off: PRD should state profiles are signed and verified at fetch-time in runtime; publish permissions restricted to Applied ML group with approval workflow; all enable/disable actions produce audit log entries. Also call out threat model link in 'Risks' section.

2025-02-07 (Aditya Rao): Action items before we mark Done: (1) finalize beta eligibility/allowlist proposal with Nikhil + Solutions Eng; (2) explicitly define 'supported models' list for MVP and how we will expand; (3) confirm Dedicated/Private gating language. Once those are in, we can collect final sign-offs.
